correctness.rationale: The survival ratio with S(-1)=1 gives log[(1-h(k+1))/(1-h(k))]=B_k-tD_k, including k=0. B_k>0 and concavity gives D_k<=0 when beta<=1. For beta>1, express D_k via the triangular second-difference kernel. The two adjacent kernels after multiplying by x^(beta-2) have likelihood ratio increasing from zero through (x-k-1)/(k+2-x) to infinity. Tilting by x^epsilon increases the adjacent D ratio strictly; the integrals near zero are finite because w(x)=x there. At beta=1+ the limiting d_k satisfies B_k/d_k=E[g(k+U)] with g(x)=x/(x+1)^2 and density for U proportional to w(u)/(k+u). For k>=1 this expectation strictly decreases as k increases: the density shifts stochastically right and g is decreasing on that range. This proves strict tail threshold descent. The independently computed rational comparisons d1/d0<2/5<B1/B0 and B2/d2<1/5<B0/d0, with d0=2 log 2 and d2=10 log 2-6 log 3, prove the initial inversion at beta=1+ and T2<T0 for all beta>1 by the ratio monotonicity. D1/D0 tends to infinity, so there is one crossing. T0 and T1 are the only possible coincident thresholds, giving exactly the stated length-three plateau. In the open two-turn region T0<t<T1 all indices k>=2 have positive increments. At t=T0<T1 the signs begin zero, negative, positive; at t=T1>T0 they begin positive, zero, positive. At beta=beta_c, T0=T1, so threshold descent from index zero is non-strict at that one pair. The exact comparison in RESULT.md governs all ties. The kernel asymptotics give T_k~1/[beta(beta-1)k^beta], and bracketing the first k with T_k<=t between neighboring thresholds yields the stated index limit for fixed beta>1. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/checks/hazard_endpoints.py exactly verifies the two logarithmic comparisons and reproduces the critical decimals (bisection is diagnostic, not the uniqueness proof). This documentation discrepancy does not affect the analytic result or the independent exact comparisons.

evidence: The DGBH index hit is this same frozen record. The Rayleigh–Weibull Finding uses P(X>=n)=q^[(exp(t n^beta)-1)^2] and its thresholds decrease even from index zero, with no increasing-then-decreasing step. The Marshall–Olkin Finding uses a tilted length-biased exponential and thresholds C_n(t) given by an exponential divided by a cubic; its two-turn window follows a different boundary. The published DGBH equations (2)–(3) give the exact survival in the submission; the bound record distinguishes the exponentiated Burr–Hatke CDF from this survival construction.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same-day non-self results share the sign-of-second-differences method and, for the Marshall–Olkin record, two-turn behavior. They neither study the same survival nor establish T0=T1 at the DGBH crossing; no priority inference follows from their dates. The logarithmic denominator and the power in the exponent together distinguish DGBH from the two inspected alternative survival constructions. The exponentiated Burr–Hatke comparison is limited by unavailable full text.
